subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` permanently fail closed on legacy ownerless rows, matching `sessions.delete`, even though those rows cannot be safely attributed or automatically migrated?
rationale: Allowing a plugin to adopt an ownerless row preserves compatibility but weakens the cross-plugin boundary; rejecting it can break older plugin-created sessions and therefore needs an explicit security and upgrade decision.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patch access to ownerless rows and leave operator or non-plugin clients as the recovery path.

options.title: Add an explicit migration
options.body: Design an authoritative operator claim or migration flow before enforcing the owner requirement on legacy rows.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patch access to ownerless rows and leave operator or non-plugin clients as the recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: Introduced the current plugin-runtime ownership fence and session projection behavior being extended.
